jobs.title: Regional Environmental Engineer, AWS Environmental Team
jobs.description:
Description

Join a diverse, dynamic, and enthusiastic team of environmental professionals who play a leading role in environmental permitting and compliance at Amazon Web Services (AWS), where we have a history of leading the world in innovative technologies and services. The work of our Regional Environmental Engineers is critical to enabling AWS's growth in the US and around the world.

The AWS Environmental team is an expanding and dynamic team that is critical to enabling AWS’s growth around the world, as well as ensuring compliance of AWS’s global operations, including physical data centers, as well as other AWS facilities, customer-facing enterprises and products. The team has responsibility for architecting and implementing AWS’s global environmental programs. This includes defining and implementing risk management and compliance systems and driving their continuous improvement; setting and refining global policies and procedures; overseeing the development of standards, tools, auditing and metrics, and employee training; ensuring effective engagement by environmental teams on global initiatives, including those that are part of Amazon’s ambitious sustainability goals; providing specialist expertise; and engaging with all AWS business units to provide scalable and effective compliance strategies that support current and future business objectives while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.

You will partner with AWS stakeholders to develop regional and site-specific development strategies enabling the construction and operation of AWS datacenters and infrastructure. You will lead environmental due diligence for site selection and acquisition, develop and execute regional and site-specific environmental permitting strategies, support environmental compliance during design and construction, and prepare for data center operations. This role requires regular engagement throughout the development lifecycle with multiple AWS stakeholders including Real Estate, Legal, Risk, Water, Design, Public Policy, Construction, and Operational teams, as well as external stakeholders including regulatory agencies, consultants, and contractors.

A successful candidate in this role will have a proven track record of delivering multiple, high-priority projects with tight timelines that require strong communication with partner teams, outside consultants and counsel, and regulatory agencies. The candidate must have a strong understanding of multi-media United States environmental permitting, remediation, and compliance requirements associated with large-scale infrastructure including experience with Clean Water Act (CWA) 404 and NPDES permitting.

Key job responsibilities

Assess environmental risks and requirements and develop mitigations and strategies to support data center siting and development strategies and site-specific project delivery.
Lead technical aspects of environmental due diligence, including Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments, regulatory and permitting evaluations, natural, biological and cultural resource evaluations, and noise assessments.
Deliver environmental permits, approvals, and plans to enable on-time and compliant construction and operations for new data center locations and expansion of existing sites.
Communicate environmental requirements, risks, and activities to internal and external project partners.
Coordinate with partner teams including Real Estate, Design, Water, Legal, Risk, Power, and others to optimize site designs to consider natural resource or operational constraints.
Develop site development and permitting strategies that are environmentally responsible and sustainable while meeting project timelines.
Lead regulatory agency interactions and negotiations in support of environmental permit acquisition and regional development strategies.
Develop, manage and track metrics to evaluate project success

About The Team

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

About AWS

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic Qualifications

Experience in MS Excel, Word, and Windows Operating Systems
5+ years of project management in data centers or comparable critical infrastructure experience
Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related field
Experience delivering multi-media environmental due diligence, permitting, and compliance projects with specific expertise in CWA 404 and NPDES permitting, groundwater protection, wastewater discharge, and natural and cultural resource evaluations

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of critical data center equipment
Experience managing and/or supporting community/public interactions.

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. jobs.title: Sr. Regional Enviro Engineer -Water Compliance, AWS Environmental Team
jobs.description:
Description

As a Regional Environmental Engineer (REE) specializing in water compliance, you will support water-related environmental compliance at AWS data centers. You will provide technical expertise in permitting and compliance across National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES), Significant Industrial User (SIU) discharge, potable water systems, groundwater wells, onsite wastewater treatment systems, stormwater, and water-quality monitoring and reporting. You will evaluate existing and proposed infrastructure, develop scalable compliance programs and technical standards, monitor environmental performance, and partner with design, construction, operations, and other stakeholders to incorporate water-related regulatory requirements into site design and operation.

Key job responsibilities

Lead water compliance programs for water supply and discharge across US data center locations
Develop and maintain the water compliance program that guides how sites and REEs obtain, renew, modify, interpret, and implement NPDES and other water discharge permits under the Clean Water Act, 40 CFR Part 122, and applicable state regulations, and translate effluent limitations, monitoring, operating, reporting, and notification requirements into site-level compliance programs
Provide guidance on evaluating regulatory applicability and permitting requirements for new sites, expansions, operational changes, and new or modified discharges
Provide guidance on evaluating industrial wastewater and stormwater permitting and compliance, including federal pretreatment under 40 CFR Part 403, local sewer-use ordinances, POTW requirements, pollution-prevention plans, inspections, best management practices, monitoring, and reporting
Provide technical guidance on potable water systems and onsite wastewater systems, including design, operation, monitoring, and compliance under applicable drinking-water and septic requirements
Develop standard templates and technical guidance for water-quality sampling and monitoring plans, review site plans, and set standards for sampling equipment, monitoring systems, and analytical methods under 40 CFR Part 136
Evaluate water and wastewater treatment processes, system performance, waste-stream characterization, water balances, and discharge pathways to determine permitting and compliance implications
Build the mechanisms, dashboards, and metrics that track water-quality data, lab reports, DMRs, and compliance performance, and support sites in identifying trends, exceedances, corrective actions, and forecasting across sites
Read and evaluate engineering plans, process-flow diagrams, P&IDs, and specifications, and partner with design, engineering, construction, and operations teams to build water-related controls into current and future designs early
Clearly communicate the technical and regulatory basis for environmental requirements and influence partner teams to implement compliant, practical, and scalable solutions
Set the standards and oversight mechanisms that keep work by employees, contractors, and consultants aligned with applicable environmental requirements and Amazon standards
Support REEs and sites in their interactions with regulatory agencies, utilities, POTWs, consultants, and contractors, and engage directly on program-level matters
Support time-critical regulatory notifications, permit applications, and monitoring reports, and support emergency response planning and incident investigations, including root causes and corrective and preventive actions
Develop and deliver water compliance training for relevant staff
Stay current with evolving water regulations and industry best practices for domestic and non-contact cooling, particularly in the data center sector

About The Team

The AWS Environmental is a team of professionals responsible for the environmental planning, delivery, and operational compliance of all AWS global infrastructure projects.

Basic Qualifications

Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
Bachelor's degree in engineering, environmental science, chemistry, or a related technical field.
Experience with NPDES and industrial wastewater permitting and compliance, including interpreting effluent limitations, sampling/monitoring requirements, reporting obligations, and noncompliance notification requirements under the Clean Water Act, 40 CFR Part 122, and federal pretreatment requirements under 40 CFR Part 403, and applicable state or local regulatory programs.
Experience developing or implementing water-quality sampling and monitoring programs, including sampling plans, sampling locations, analytical parameters and methods, sampling equipment, laboratory coordination, and data evaluation.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in engineering or equivalent.
Experience supporting water compliance across multiple facilities, jurisdictions, or regulatory programs, and with public water system requirements under the Safe Drinking Water Act, 40 CFR Part 141, and applicable state drinking-water programs.
Working knowledge of potable water and septic/onsite wastewater treatment systems, including their design, operation, monitoring, and regulatory compliance.
Experience with industrial wastewater treatment, pretreatment systems, publicly owned treatment works, and local industrial-user permits, including evaluating the design and operation of water and wastewater treatment, conveyance, storage, sampling, and monitoring systems.
Experience reviewing civil, mechanical, plumbing, and process designs for water-related regulatory and permit compliance.
Experience developing scalable environmental standards, procedures, tools, or compliance mechanisms for use across multiple sites, and managing multiple technically complex projects and regulatory deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Strong analytical, technical-writing, communication, relationship-building, influencing, and negotiation skills.

Description

As a Regional Environmental Engineer (REE) specializing in water compliance, you will support water-related environmental compliance at AWS data centers. You will provide technical expertise in permitting and compliance across National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES), Significant Industrial User (SIU) discharge, potable water systems, groundwater wells, onsite wastewater treatment systems, stormwater, and water-quality monitoring and reporting. You will evaluate existing and proposed infrastructure, develop scalable compliance programs and technical standards, monitor environmental performance, and partner with design, construction, operations, and other stakeholders to incorporate water-related regulatory requirements into site design and operation.

Key job responsibilities

Lead water compliance programs for water supply and discharge across US data center locations
Develop and maintain the water compliance program that guides how sites and REEs obtain, renew, modify, interpret, and implement NPDES and other water discharge permits under the Clean Water Act, 40 CFR Part 122, and applicable state regulations, and translate effluent limitations, monitoring, operating, reporting, and notification requirements into site-level compliance programs
Provide guidance on evaluating regulatory applicability and permitting requirements for new sites, expansions, operational changes, and new or modified discharges
Provide guidance on evaluating industrial wastewater and stormwater permitting and compliance, including federal pretreatment under 40 CFR Part 403, local sewer-use ordinances, POTW requirements, pollution-prevention plans, inspections, best management practices, monitoring, and reporting
Provide technical guidance on potable water systems and onsite wastewater systems, including design, operation, monitoring, and compliance under applicable drinking-water and septic requirements
Develop standard templates and technical guidance for water-quality sampling and monitoring plans, review site plans, and set standards for sampling equipment, monitoring systems, and analytical methods under 40 CFR Part 136
Evaluate water and wastewater treatment processes, system performance, waste-stream characterization, water balances, and discharge pathways to determine permitting and compliance implications
Build the mechanisms, dashboards, and metrics that track water-quality data, lab reports, DMRs, and compliance performance, and support sites in identifying trends, exceedances, corrective actions, and forecasting across sites
Read and evaluate engineering plans, process-flow diagrams, P&IDs, and specifications, and partner with design, engineering, construction, and operations teams to build water-related controls into current and future designs early
Clearly communicate the technical and regulatory basis for environmental requirements and influence partner teams to implement compliant, practical, and scalable solutions
Set the standards and oversight mechanisms that keep work by employees, contractors, and consultants aligned with applicable environmental requirements and Amazon standards
Support REEs and sites in their interactions with regulatory agencies, utilities, POTWs, consultants, and contractors, and engage directly on program-level matters
Support time-critical regulatory notifications, permit applications, and monitoring reports, and support emergency response planning and incident investigations, including root causes and corrective and preventive actions
Develop and deliver water compliance training for relevant staff
Stay current with evolving water regulations and industry best practices for domestic and non-contact cooling, particularly in the data center sector

About The Team

The AWS Environmental is a team of professionals responsible for the environmental planning, delivery, and operational compliance of all AWS global infrastructure projects.

Basic Qualifications

Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
Bachelor's degree in engineering, environmental science, chemistry, or a related technical field.
Experience with NPDES and industrial wastewater permitting and compliance, including interpreting effluent limitations, sampling/monitoring requirements, reporting obligations, and noncompliance notification requirements under the Clean Water Act, 40 CFR Part 122, and federal pretreatment requirements under 40 CFR Part 403, and applicable state or local regulatory programs.
Experience developing or implementing water-quality sampling and monitoring programs, including sampling plans, sampling locations, analytical parameters and methods, sampling equipment, laboratory coordination, and data evaluation.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in engineering or equivalent.
Experience supporting water compliance across multiple facilities, jurisdictions, or regulatory programs, and with public water system requirements under the Safe Drinking Water Act, 40 CFR Part 141, and applicable state drinking-water programs.
Working knowledge of potable water and septic/onsite wastewater treatment systems, including their design, operation, monitoring, and regulatory compliance.
Experience with industrial wastewater treatment, pretreatment systems, publicly owned treatment works, and local industrial-user permits, including evaluating the design and operation of water and wastewater treatment, conveyance, storage, sampling, and monitoring systems.
Experience reviewing civil, mechanical, plumbing, and process designs for water-related regulatory and permit compliance.
Experience developing scalable environmental standards, procedures, tools, or compliance mechanisms for use across multiple sites, and managing multiple technically complex projects and regulatory deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Strong analytical, technical-writing, communication, relationship-building, influencing, and negotiation skills.

All Riverside Research opportunities require U.S. Citizenship.

We are seeking a skilled Remote Sensing Engineer
to support the development, analysis, and exploitation of remote sensing data for national security, defense, and geospatial intelligence missions. The ideal candidate has experience working with geospatial datasets, remote sensing technologies, and automation tools, and is comfortable collaborating across multidisciplinary teams to solve complex technical challenges.

An active Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) clearance is required
for this position.

Responsibilities

Process, analyze, and interpret satellite, airborne, and other remotely sensed imagery.
Develop and maintain geospatial analysis workflows and automated processing pipelines.
Design and implement Python-based tools to support imagery processing, feature extraction, and geospatial analysis.
Perform image classification, object detection, change detection, and spatial analysis using commercial and open-source tools.
Support sensor calibration, validation, and quality assurance activities.
Work closely with engineers, data scientists, and intelligence analysts to develop mission-focused solutions.
Prepare technical documentation, reports, and presentations for technical and non-technical audiences.
Evaluate emerging remote sensing technologies and recommend improvements to existing workflows.
Contribute to project planning, technical discussions, and continuous process improvement initiatives.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Active TS/SCI security clearance (required).
Bachelor's degree in Remote Sensing, Geospatial Science, Geography, GIS, Computer Science, Engineering, Physics, Environmental Science, or a related technical discipline.
minimum of 5 years professional experience in remote sensing, geospatial analysis, GIS, or a related engineering field.
Experience processing and analyzing satellite, aerial, or other remotely sensed imagery.
Proficiency with remote sensing and GIS software such as ArcGIS Pro, QGIS, ENVI, ERDAS Imagine, or similar platforms.
Strong Python programming skills for geospatial analysis and workflow automation.
Experience with geospatial libraries such as GDAL, Rasterio, GeoPandas, Shapely, or OpenCV.
Understanding of raster and vector geospatial data formats and coordinate reference systems.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently in a remote, collaborative environment.

Experience supporting DoD, NGA, NRO, or Intelligence Community programs.
Experience with SAR, LiDAR, hyperspectral, multispectral, or thermal imagery.
Familiarity with cloud-based geospatial processing environments such as AWS or Azure.
Experience with machine learning or computer vision techniques applied to geospatial imagery.
Knowledge of containerization technologies such as Docker and modern software development practices.
Experience with Git and collaborative software development workflows.

You will contribute your technical expertise in the management of Protected Sites by :

Undertaking the d irect regulation of Protected Sites through the assenting and consenting of activities.
Securing the effective proactive management of Protected Sites through the provision of advice and guidance, and by developing management agreements and partnerships.
Providing specialist advice to internal teams, functions and Directorates, and contributing to the direct or partnership delivery of projects and mitigation schemes that protect and improve the environment.

This is an exciting opportunity to apply your conservation expertise in a varied role that combines regulatory work, partnership development and the delivery of practical environmental outcomes.

Driving is essential to this role. Due to the remote nature of many locations and limited public transport links, there is no practical alternative to travelling by vehicle. You must hold a full, current UK driving licence.

As an organisation we support flexible working. You will be contracted to an NRW office within the place base / location above and a suitable hybrid working pattern will be agreed on appointment. Any regular face to face meetings or training will be planned in advance.

To make an informal enquiry about this role, please contact Arfon Hughes
at Arfon.Hughes@cyfoethnaturiolcymru.gov.uk

Interviews will be face to face
on 15/10/2026
(details of location will be shared in advance)

About Us

The Dwyfor & Meirionnydd Environment Team is responsible for the management of 136 Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs). Our area stretches from the upland landscapes of Cadair Idris, Migneint Arenig and Dduallt & Rhiniogydd, down the tributaries of the Dyfi, Mawddach, Dwyryd and Glaslyn, to the coastline from Aberdyfi to Trefor near Caernarfon.

It is a significant area of land, renowned for its outstanding habitats and stunning scenery.

What You Will Do

Work with a wide range of internal and external, specifically , landowners, businesses, public bodies, recreation groups, volunteers and third sector organisations to enable others to achieve SMNR.
Establish, maintain and advise partners to support the development of partnership projects and plans through from concepts to implementation. These projects will deliver outcomes aligned with place priorities.
Assess compliance with relevant legislation, assent or consent conditions. Where non-compliance is identified, determine and implement the most appropriate intervention option to ensure recovery of the Protected site features and a return to compliance as quickly as possible. Take appropriate actions to collect evidence for enforcement purposes, in accordance with defined procedures.
Draft valid consents and assents for operations affecting protected sites. For all work areas produce required advice, investigations, documentation and reports to agreed quality standards to support operational and management decisions, protected site notification, public enquiries, court cases etc so that information, evidence and NRW interests are accurately and effectively presented.
Within your area of expertise, provide professional local advice and responses to consultations from planning and permitting teams. Maintain working relationships with these teams through regular liaison.
Monitor progress of work, which may include interpretation of data, contractor management, project delivery or compliance with management agreements or statutory legal notices. Identify and support any remedial actions to ensure outcome delivery.
Play a role in a resilient NRW Incident Management Service that follows NRW process to ensure effective, timely and safe response to incidents.
Undertake health and safety duties and responsibilities appropriate to the post
Be committed to Natural Resources Wales Equal Opportunities and Diversity Policy , together with an understanding of how it operates within the responsibilities of the post
Be committed to your own development through the effective use of your personal development plan (known as Sgwrs).
Required to take part in incident response activities.
Any other reasonable duties requested commensurate with the grade of this role.

Your qualifications, experience, knowledge and skills

In your application and interview you will be asked to demonstrate the following skills and experience using the STAR method.

Degree level qualification or the equivalent level of knowledge in ecology, conservation or biodiversity.
An understanding of how multi-functional teams contribute to the Sustainable Management of Natural Resources (SMNR) and the wider objectives and responsibilities of NRW
Ensure continuing professional and personal development, expertise and competence through formal and informal learning and certification.
Strong and effective self-management and organisational skills.
The ability to influence, negotiate and gain cooperation of others including experience of dealing successfully with difficult people or situations and proven ability to work well as part of a team. The ability to use specialised IT systems, such as GIS or NRW customised applications.
Hold a current full UK valid licence to drive NRW fleet vehicles. (cars and vans)

Essential: Level C2 - Higher proficiency level

Welsh language levels

If you do not meet the Welsh language level requirements for this role your application will not be shortlisted.

Further details on eligibility can be found on National security vetting: clearance levels - GOV.UK . Offers will also be subject to a satisfactory Disclosure and Barring Service Check (DBS) check.

This encompasses responsibility for a broad range of municipal infrastructure and services, including transportation and fleet services, parks, roads, and rural operations, water and wastewater treatment, underground services, solid waste, infrastructure maintenance, and environmental technical services.

The Executive Director plays a pivotal role in advancing the Municipality’s integrated service delivery strategy and ensuring that municipal operations are effective, efficient, and aligned with strategic priorities. This role encompasses leadership of complex, multi-disciplinary municipal services and programs, fostering collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement. The Executive Director provides professional advice to the CAO and Council, ensures applicable resolutions, bylaws, policies and plans of Council are implemented, and keeps the CAO and Council informed on progress and emerging issues.

Responsibilities

As a leader, the incumbent upholds the Municipality’s organizational values and is accountable for fostering a healthy, safe, respectful, and inclusive workplace. Leading by example, the Executive Director promotes the Municipality’s cultural competencies of personal accountability, continuous improvement, effective communication, collaboration, excellence in customer service, and support for common goals. Primary responsibilities of this position include:

Strategic Leadership

Contributes to the overall leadership and strategic direction of the Municipality as a key member of the senior leadership team.
Aligns divisional strategies with Council priorities and the Municipality’s long-term vision, ensuring services are delivered with integrity, transparency, and responsiveness.
Provides expert advice to the CAO, Council, and senior leadership, and collaborates across departments to identify and advance both short-term and long-term strategic priorities.
Fosters a culture of innovation, sustainability, and continuous improvement across all assigned portfolio areas.

Operational Oversight

Provides oversight of the Public Works and Environmental Services portfolios, aligning operations with strategic priorities, community values, and regulatory requirements.
Promotes responsible stewardship of municipal infrastructure and assets through effective governance, planning, and risk management.
Tracks and analyzes major operational issues, providing timely updates, strategic insights, and recommendations to the CAO and, when appropriate, Council.
Drives operational excellence through data-informed decision-making, continuous improvement, and process optimization.
Leads the resolution of complex or high-impact operational challenges, ensuring cross-functional collaboration and engagement.
Anticipates emerging trends and risks, proactively adapting operations to meet future community and organizational needs.
Fosters a culture of accountability, innovation, and service excellence across all operational areas.
Champions complex or difficult public works and environmental services projects.

Engagement and Community Relations

Creates positive working relationships with Council, municipal administration, employees, residents, Indigenous groups, regional partners, and other collaborators to meet shared objectives.
Represents the Municipality’s interests in Council meetings, public forums, intergovernmental meetings, and community consultations.
Demonstrates consistent, effective, and meaningful engagement with respect to Truth and Reconciliation and the Calls to Action that the Municipality has identified for implementation.
Effectively handles disputes or complaints involving citizens and other interest groups.

People Leadership

Builds and leads a high-performing team of directors, managers, and staff, fostering a culture of excellence and accountability.
Establishes a clear vision for success, ensuring teams have the resources and support needed to achieve strategic goals.
Develops and implements performance measures with defined objectives and measurable outcomes.
Champions innovation and leads organizational change, empowering staff to enhance municipal service and operational delivery.
Models municipal values and cultivates an inclusive, respectful workplace that prioritizes diversity, equity, inclusion, and psychological and physical safety.
Ensures the Public Works and Environmental Services portfolio is appropriately structured and staffed to deliver safe, reliable, and efficient municipal infrastructure and environmental services.

The Dwyfor & Meirionnydd Environment Team is responsible for the management of 136 Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs). Join a diverse, dynamic, and enthusiastic team of environmental professionals who play a leading role in environmental permitting and compliance at Amazon Web Services (AWS), where we have a history of leading the world in innovative technologies and services. The work of our Regional Environmental Engineers is critical to enabling AWS's growth in the US and around the world.

The AWS Environmental team is an expanding and dynamic team that is critical to enabling AWS’s growth around the world, as well as ensuring compliance of AWS’s global operations, including physical data centers, as well as other AWS facilities, customer-facing enterprises and products. The team has responsibility for architecting and implementing AWS’s global environmental programs. This includes defining and implementing risk management and compliance systems and driving their continuous improvement; setting and refining global policies and procedures; overseeing the development of standards, tools, auditing and metrics, and employee training; ensuring effective engagement by environmental teams on global initiatives, including those that are part of Amazon’s ambitious sustainability goals; providing specialist expertise; and engaging with all AWS business units to provide scalable and effective compliance strategies that support current and future business objectives while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.

You will partner with AWS stakeholders to develop regional and site-specific development strategies enabling the construction and operation of AWS datacenters and infrastructure. You will lead environmental due diligence for site selection and acquisition, develop and execute regional and site-specific environmental permitting strategies, support environmental compliance during design and construction, and prepare for data center operations. This role requires regular engagement throughout the development lifecycle with multiple AWS stakeholders including Real Estate, Legal, Risk, Water, Design, Public Policy, Construction, and Operational teams, as well as external stakeholders including regulatory agencies, consultants, and contractors.

A successful candidate in this role will have a proven track record of delivering multiple, high-priority projects with tight timelines that require strong communication with partner teams, outside consultants and counsel, and regulatory agencies. The candidate must have a strong understanding of multi-media United States environmental permitting, remediation, and compliance requirements associated with large-scale infrastructure including experience with Clean Water Act (CWA) 404 and NPDES permitting.

Assess environmental risks and requirements and develop mitigations and strategies to support data center siting and development strategies and site-specific project delivery.
Lead technical aspects of environmental due diligence, including Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments, regulatory and permitting evaluations, natural, biological and cultural resource evaluations, and noise assessments.

Communicate environmental requirements, risks, and activities to internal and external project partners.
Coordinate with partner teams including Real Estate, Design, Water, Legal, Risk, Power, and others to optimize site designs to consider natural resource or operational constraints.

And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Experience in MS Excel, Word, and Windows Operating Systems
5+ years of project management in data centers or comparable critical infrastructure experience
Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related field
Experience delivering multi-media environmental due diligence, permitting, and compliance projects with specific expertise in CWA 404 and NPDES permitting, groundwater protection, wastewater discharge, and natural and cultural resource evaluations

Experience developing or implementing water-quality sampling and monitoring programs, including sampling plans, sampling locations, analytical parameters and methods, sampling equipment, laboratory coordination, and data evaluation.

Experience supporting water compliance across multiple facilities, jurisdictions, or regulatory programs, and with public water system requirements under the Safe Drinking Water Act, 40 CFR Part 141, and applicable state drinking-water programs.

What You Will Do

Work with a wide range of internal and external, specifically , landowners, businesses, public bodies, recreation groups, volunteers and third sector organisations to enable others to achieve SMNR.
Establish, maintain and advise partners to support the development of partnership projects and plans through from concepts to implementation. These projects will deliver outcomes aligned with place priorities.
Assess compliance with relevant legislation, assent or consent conditions. Take appropriate actions to collect evidence for enforcement purposes, in accordance with defined procedures.
Draft valid consents and assents for operations affecting protected sites. For all work areas produce required advice, investigations, documentation and reports to agreed quality standards to support operational and management decisions, protected site notification, public enquiries, court cases etc so that information, evidence and NRW interests are accurately and effectively presented.

Play a role in a resilient NRW Incident Management Service that follows NRW process to ensure effective, timely and safe response to incidents.
Undertake health and safety duties and responsibilities appropriate to the post
Be committed to Natural Resources Wales Equal Opportunities and Diversity Policy , together with an understanding of how it operates within the responsibilities of the post

Required to take part in incident response activities.
Any other reasonable duties requested commensurate with the grade of this role.

Degree level qualification or the equivalent level of knowledge in ecology, conservation or biodiversity.
An understanding of how multi-functional teams contribute to the Sustainable Management of Natural Resources (SMNR) and the wider objectives and responsibilities of NRW
Ensure continuing professional and personal development, expertise and competence through formal and informal learning and certification.
Strong and effective self-management and organisational skills.
The ability to influence, negotiate and gain cooperation of others including experience of dealing successfully with difficult people or situations and proven ability to work well as part of a team. The ability to use specialised IT systems, such as GIS or NRW customised applications.
Hold a current full UK valid licence to drive NRW fleet vehicles. (cars and vans)

Welsh language levels

Further details on eligibility can be found on National security vetting: clearance levels - GOV.UK . Offers will also be subject to a satisfactory Disclosure and Barring Service Check (DBS) check.

generous leave entitlements for all your life needs

Reporting to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the Executive Director, Public Works and Environmental Services is a senior leader that provides strategic direction, vision, and oversight across the Municipality’s Public Works and Environmental Services portfolios. This encompasses responsibility for a broad range of municipal infrastructure and services, including transportation and fleet services, parks, roads, and rural operations, water and wastewater treatment, underground services, solid waste, infrastructure maintenance, and environmental technical services.

The Executive Director plays a pivotal role in advancing the Municipality’s integrated service delivery strategy and ensuring that municipal operations are effective, efficient, and aligned with strategic priorities. This role encompasses leadership of complex, multi-disciplinary municipal services and programs, fostering collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement. The Executive Director provides professional advice to the CAO and Council, ensures applicable resolutions, bylaws, policies and plans of Council are implemented, and keeps the CAO and Council informed on progress and emerging issues.

Responsibilities

As a leader, the incumbent upholds the Municipality’s organizational values and is accountable for fostering a healthy, safe, respectful, and inclusive workplace. Leading by example, the Executive Director promotes the Municipality’s cultural competencies of personal accountability, continuous improvement, effective communication, collaboration, excellence in customer service, and support for common goals. Primary responsibilities of this position include:

Strategic Leadership

Contributes to the overall leadership and strategic direction of the Municipality as a key member of the senior leadership team.
Aligns divisional strategies with Council priorities and the Municipality’s long-term vision, ensuring services are delivered with integrity, transparency, and responsiveness.
Provides expert advice to the CAO, Council, and senior leadership, and collaborates across departments to identify and advance both short-term and long-term strategic priorities.
Fosters a culture of innovation, sustainability, and continuous improvement across all assigned portfolio areas.

Operational Oversight

Provides oversight of the Public Works and Environmental Services portfolios, aligning operations with strategic priorities, community values, and regulatory requirements.
Promotes responsible stewardship of municipal infrastructure and assets through effective governance, planning, and risk management.
Tracks and analyzes major operational issues, providing timely updates, strategic insights, and recommendations to the CAO and, when appropriate, Council.
Drives operational excellence through data-informed decision-making, continuous improvement, and process optimization.
Leads the resolution of complex or high-impact operational challenges, ensuring cross-functional collaboration and engagement.
Anticipates emerging trends and risks, proactively adapting operations to meet future community and organizational needs.
Fosters a culture of accountability, innovation, and service excellence across all operational areas.
Champions complex or difficult public works and environmental services projects.

Engagement and Community Relations

Creates positive working relationships with Council, municipal administration, employees, residents, Indigenous groups, regional partners, and other collaborators to meet shared objectives.
Represents the Municipality’s interests in Council meetings, public forums, intergovernmental meetings, and community consultations.
Demonstrates consistent, effective, and meaningful engagement with respect to Truth and Reconciliation and the Calls to Action that the Municipality has identified for implementation.
Effectively handles disputes or complaints involving citizens and other interest groups.

People Leadership

Builds and leads a high-performing team of directors, managers, and staff, fostering a culture of excellence and accountability.
Establishes a clear vision for success, ensuring teams have the resources and support needed to achieve strategic goals.
Develops and implements performance measures with defined objectives and measurable outcomes.
Champions innovation and leads organizational change, empowering staff to enhance municipal service and operational delivery.
Models municipal values and cultivates an inclusive, respectful workplace that prioritizes diversity, equity, inclusion, and psychological and physical safety.
Ensures the Public Works and Environmental Services portfolio is appropriately structured and staffed to deliver safe, reliable, and efficient municipal infrastructure and environmental services.
Applies sound human resource practices to inspire high performance and support employee development.

Financial and Administrative Management

Leads divisional planning and budgeting, ensuring fiscal responsibility and proactively addressing long-term financial needs.
Supports and collaborates with the CAO and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to develop the annual budget and advises on divisional priorities.
Oversees and monitors divisional financial activities, ensuring effective controls and sound fiscal management.
Upholds compliance with all relevant laws, regulations, and municipal standards.
Supports and collaborates on the Municipality’s asset management strategy to ensure sustainable and strategic use of municipal resources.

Emergency Management Leadership

Proactively prepares for and provides divisional leadership during major events, including operational disruptions, emergencies, and disasters.
Ensures the development, maintenance, staff familiarization, and activation of business continuity plans across all assigned operational areas. Participates as a member of the Muncipality’s Emergency Management Agency (EMA) as appointed by the CAO, to support the EMA’s duties and functions.
Provides recommendations to the CAO regarding policies, programs, and budgetary requirements to sustain and improve the Emergency Management Plan (EMP).
Collaborates with the EMA and other departments to ensure the protection of critical infrastructure is integrated into emergency preparedness, continuity planning, and response strategies.
Reviews findings from Post-Event Action Reports and approves recommendations, as necessary, to strengthen future response and recovery efforts.
Engages with internal and external partners to ensure collaboration, alignment, and community resilience.

Skills Requirements

Candidates need to show evidence of the following:
Sound knowledge of and demonstrated proficiency in public works (transportation, fleet, and parks, roads, and rural operations) and environmental services (water treatment and distribution, wastewater collection and treatment, and solid waste management).
Proven expertise in strategic leadership, project and program management, asset management, organizational planning, and service delivery optimization within a complex municipal environment.
Strong understanding of municipal legislation, infrastructure planning, environmental stewardship, and applicable regulatory and compliance frameworks.
Sound understanding of municipal government administration and the Municipal Government Act.
Broad knowledge of current affairs, municipal, provincial, and federal politics.
Demonstrated ability to lead large, diverse teams and manage complex, multi-disciplinary operations.
A demonstrated commitment to fostering inclusive, respectful, and high-performing workplace cultures.
Ability to provide leadership and build relationships with Council and various groups including but not limited to industry, government, Indigenous groups, and members of the public.
Expertise in strategic issues management and policy development.
Experience introducing transformational change in a highly complex and evolving organization serving a rapidly changing community.
Ability to communicate effectively and transparently with all parties to build trust and accountability.
Excellent interpersonal, problem-solving, negotiation, facilitation, and mediation skills.
High political acumen and ability to anticipate politically sensitive issues.

Education

Degree in Public or Business Administration, Engineering, Environmental Science, or related field is required.
Certifications in any of the following are considered assets: Water Distribution, Water Collection, Water Treatment, Landfill Operations, or SWANA.
An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

Experience

Fifteen (15) years of progressively responsible leadership experience in public works, environmental services, utilities, and/or municipal operations, is required. This experience must encompass the management of complex, multi-disciplinary operations; the ability to synthesize and act on large volumes of information; sound decision-making in complex and ambiguous situations; effective negotiation; budget administration and control; and the development of innovative solutions to operational and community issues.
Experience working in a public sector environment with unionized and non-unionized employees is an asset.
